clue.text: Womaniser, as no other, is into sparkling wine

indicators.note: 'is into' tells us the shuffled letters sit inside the wine

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: 'other' asks for the letters of 'as no' to be made other than they are, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A notorious ladies' man, like nobody else, has developed a taste for fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' turns AS NO into SANO, and 'is into' places SANO inside CAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was the famous Venetian seducer, so his name is used for any serial seducer of women.

clue.text: Gobsmacked when port's said to be lacking fruit

parts.note: port is the side of a ship on your hand nearest the heart when facing forward, so 'port's' gives that side plus S

indicators.note: 'said to be' signals that the next words are only heard, not spelt

parts.note: without a peach, i.e. peachless

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned to hear that a harbour town has run out of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' makes PEACHLESS sound like PEECHLESS; joined to LEFTS the whole run of letters is LEFT SPEECHLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gobsmacked is being astounded, so stunned that words fail you.

clue.text: Yelped, getting wound up and most indignant

parts.note: the clue word is itself what the first nine letters produce when read as an instruction: a six-letter word followed by 'off' as its anagram signal
something wound up has come to an end, i.e. ended

explanation.surface: Someone yelps, getting worked up and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: the first nine letters, read as an instruction, say 'DEEPLY, off', and an anagram of DEEPLY is the clue's 'Yelped'. 'Wound up' looks like 'annoyed' but means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deeply offended is to feel the strongest indignation at an insult.

clue.text: Frightened by gangster with gun

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL
carrying a gun is being armed

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified by a mobster carrying a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed and frightened are synonyms, both meaning scared.

clue.text: Extra problem with drugs, when losing heart

indicators.note: 'losing heart' means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: addiction is a dependence on drugs

explanation.surface: An additional difficulty: drug dependence, made worse by losing the will to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when losing heart' removes C, the middle letter of ADDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something extra, added on to what was there.

clue.text: Bully gets personal after I'd left

indicators.note: 'gets' here stands for the inner piece being taken in

parts.note: intimate means personal, private
the contraction I'd, written as its two letters

explanation.surface: A tormentor starts making it personal once I've gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue actually runs backwards: 'after I'd left' says that when ID leaves the answer, what remains is INTIMATE, 'personal'. The parse shows the equivalent forward route, ID inside INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to frighten them into submission, to cow them with threats.

clue.text: 23 24 across in a good way, that is

parts.note: doing something well is doing it in a good way
i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A cross-reference pointing to the rubber footwear, done nicely, that is.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 24 across' is the long rubber footwear at those entries, of which this is the everyday British shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is the informal name for a rubber knee-length waterproof boot.

clue.text: In autumn, we're suffering for so long!

indicators.note: 'In' places the shuffled letters inside the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: 'suffering' suggests the letters of we're are in distress, i.e. knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that, in autumn, they suffer for such a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' turns WERE into REWE, and 'In' places it inside FALL. 'so long!' reads as a complaint but is a parting phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So long!' is an informal goodbye, a parting greeting.

clue.text: Dire peril

parts.note: the word dire splits as D plus IRE, and ire is anger

explanation.surface: A grave and terrible hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Dire' as D + IRE; swap IRE for its synonym ANGER and keep the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril and danger are synonyms, both meaning exposure to harm.

clue.text: Former role here in Paris starts on picket line, extremely shaken, drunk or stoned

definitions.note: three examples of the verb form named by the answer

parts.note: former means past or bygone
a role is a part in a play
ici is French for here

indicators.note: 'starts on' picks the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A striker's old job on the line, edgy, drunk or high, in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: shaken, drunk and stoned are all past participles, which the surface reads as states of the picketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken, drunk and stoned are each the form of a verb used after 'have' for completed action.

clue.text: See 10
Throw back then throw forward, becoming combative

indicators.note: 'back' tells us the word for throw is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
to shy is to fling something forward, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Hurling something backwards, then forwards, and turning aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes LOB into BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for awkward and argumentative, from Bolshevik.

clue.text: See 2
Brought out from the East: one in ten catching it

indicators.note: 'catching' means the reversed word holds the following one
'from the East' means reading from the right, in reverse

parts.note: a decile is one of ten equal groups in statistics

explanation.surface: Something drawn out of the Orient: a tenth part, grabbing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns DECILE into ELICED, and 'catching' puts IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit something is to draw it out, as a response or fact.

clue.text: Sausage served by the Spanish in a fancy hotel

indicators.note: 'in' places the Spanish article within the hotel name

parts.note: the Savoy is a grand luxury hotel in London
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A banger served by a Spaniard at a posh hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SAVOY is a famous luxury hotel on London's Strand.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a highly seasoned British smoked sausage, often sold in chip shops.

clue.text: See 3
They say you ultimately finish in incontinence pad, being miserable

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: 'They say' signals that a word is heard, and you is heard as the letter U

parts.note: the word you

indicators.note: 'in' puts that letter inside the pad

parts.note: a nappy is a pad for incontinence (a diaper)

indicators.note: 'ultimately' picks the final letter of the word finish

explanation.surface: Apparently you'll end up in an incontinence pad, which is depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes H from finish, and 'in' puts it into NAPPY, a British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy and miserable are synonyms, both meaning sad.

clue.text: Really thick to make poor start on simple acquisition of academic publisher

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the next
'start' takes the opening letter of the word poor
'acquisition of' means the first pieces take in the publisher

parts.note: easy means simple
OUP is Oxford University Press, an academic publisher

explanation.surface: A dim plan: a weak beginning to an easy takeover of a university press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' gives P, put 'on' EASY to make PEASY, which takes in OUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense yellow London fog, so pea-soupy describes very thick murk.

clue.text: Essentially queasy about toxic compound and strange objects

indicators.note: 'about' means the middle letters go round the mixed letters
'Essentially' takes the central letters, the essence, of queasy
'compound' asks for the letters of toxic to be mixed together

explanation.surface: Feeling sick around some poisonous chemical and other weird things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' gives EA; 'compound' turns TOXIC into XOTIC; 'about' wraps EA round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curiosities, objects that are unusual because they come from far away.

clue.text: Key point about sci-fi is not to start getting cross

indicators.note: 'about' means the key point goes round the shortened sci-fi

parts.note: the crux is the central, decisive point

indicators.note: 'not to start' drops the first letter of sci-fi

explanation.surface: The main point about science fiction is that it should never begin angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' turns SCI-FI into CIFI, which goes inside CRUX. 'cross' is a noun here, not 'angry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ.

clue.text: Referee nearly dislocated joint

indicators.note: 'dislocated' suggests letters knocked out of place, to be rearranged
'nearly' cuts off the last letter of referee

explanation.surface: The match official almost put a joint out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' gives REFERE; 'dislocated' rearranges it. 'joint' is not a body part but a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a slang term for a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: Greek having drunk nectar goes into mysterious trance

indicators.note: 'drunk' says the letters of nectar are reeling, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek who has drunk the drink of the gods falls into a strange trance.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two wordplays: 'nectar' rearranged ('drunk') and 'trance' rearranged ('mysterious') both give the answer; 'goes into' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the largest Greek island.

clue.text: Stick around at home for the dog

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer here is an adjective meaning of the dog

indicators.note: 'around' means the stick goes round the next piece

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Keep a stick at home for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts IN inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is the adjective for things relating to dogs, from Latin canis.

clue.text: Gushing in 5 about nice top footwear

parts.note: welling means gushing up, as water from a spring

indicators.note: 'about' means to boot goes round that letter

parts.note: 5 down is ADDITION, and 'in addition' means to boot

indicators.note: 'top' picks the first letter of the word nice

explanation.surface: Gushing about a nice top in a fashion review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' gives N, and 'about' sets TO BOOT round it, making TONBOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the full name of the knee-high rubber waterproof boot, named after the Duke.

clue.text: See 23
Second charge raised, causing complaint

parts.note: B is the second letter, or second class

indicators.note: in a down clue 'raised' means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A further fee goes up, provoking a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns FEE into EEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Couple's seeking to provide accommodation for tenant

indicators.note: 'to provide accommodation for' says the words house the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A pair are looking to put someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, so is a tenant.

clue.text: Name the early Muslim leaders interrupting Christian child out of familiarity

indicators.note: 'interrupting' means those letters break into the Christian

parts.note: a Copt is an Egyptian Christian

indicators.note: 'leaders' picks the opening letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Naming the first caliphs while cutting in on a Christian child.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'familiarity breeds contempt', so the answer is the offspring of familiarity.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying makes scorn the offspring that over-closeness produces.
